The upper-left panel likely shows the target arrangement: black above white. I’ll test whether the second directional action lowers the white receptacle toward the black block.

ACTION2

ACTION2 caused no puzzle change; the bottom yellow row is likely an action-budget meter. I’ll probe another discrete control before using clicks.

ACTION1

The top-right toolbar has white selected (black underline). I’ll test the likely left control to switch selection to black.

ACTION3

ACTION3 is clearly the active left/rotation control: it displaced the selected white piece up-left and tipped it counterclockwise. I’ll test the opposite control to recover and map its behavior.

ACTION4

The inverse confirms ACTION3/ACTION4 move or rotate the selected white rigid body. The goal preview requires black above white, so I’ll use the remaining discrete control to switch selection or commit.

ACTION5

The mechanic is now clear: the white dispenser fires into the nearest half of the black 10×10 target. Firing from above made the wrong white-over-black split; the goal is black-over-white. Reset, rotate the dispenser four 45° steps to below, then fire.

RESET

Rotate the dispenser counterclockwise from north to northwest (step 1 of 4 toward the south position).

ACTION3

Continue counterclockwise rotation toward the left side (step 2 of 4).

ACTION3

Repeated ACTION3 is blocked at the diagonal position, so it is not a freely repeatable rotation. Test the directional down control, which should move the white dispenser beneath the target.

ACTION2

The dispenser is now directly left of the black target. Move down once to round its lower-left corner.

ACTION2

The white container is now diagonally below-left of the black target. Move right to place it directly beneath the target, opening upward.

ACTION4

The white dispenser is aligned directly below the black target, so firing upward should create the required black-over-white split.

ACTION5

Level 2 target equals a white top-half stamp followed by a maroon lower-right diagonal stamp. The white tool is already directly above the canvas, so apply the first stamp.

ACTION5

The level appears to be in an automatic piece-spawning animation. I’ll click an unused background corner to advance time without altering the puzzle.

The editable 10×10 board at x=27–36, y=34–43 already matches the pink/black portions of the upper-left target; only the orange cells remain. First select the orange palette swatch.

Orange is selected. I’ll paint the first required cell: the top-right pixel of the 10×10 output.

ACTION6 36 35

Orange is selected; direct clicking does not paint, so the 10×10 block must be moved through the paint chamber. I’ll test the likely left-movement control to begin positioning it for a diagonal pass.

ACTION3

The left command tilted the orange paint applicator northwest of the canvas, with its open edge aimed southeast along the target diagonal. Activate it to apply the orange triangular region.

ACTION5

The orange pass produced the opposite triangular half, so I’ll restore the level and use the brush’s opposite orientation.

RESET

Reset restored the black canvas and default pink horizontal applicator. Recreate the required pink upper half with a horizontal pass.

ACTION5

The first pass correctly created the target’s white upper half over the black base. Next, select magenta for the diagonal overlay.

ACTION6 46 4

The red dye is selected. Test the right control to establish the paper’s rotation/tilt for the lower-right diagonal dip.

ACTION4

The red applicator is now angled along the target’s diagonal and positioned to coat the lower-right triangle. Apply it.

ACTION5

The clockwise angle painted the wrong diagonal (orange wide at the top instead of the bottom). Reset this level, then use the opposite rotation.

RESET

Reset restored the black canvas with the red stamp selected. First recreate the required red upper half using the horizontal stamp.

ACTION5

The red 10×5 block has landed correctly, forming the target’s red upper base over the black lower half. Next, select the yellow palette swatch before shaping the diagonal yellow overlay.

ACTION6 46 4

Yellow is selected and no paint has been applied yet. Rotate the workpiece one step left to inspect the available diagonal orientation; this is reversible before dipping.

ACTION3

The yellow tool is currently northwest of the canvas, which would paint the wrong diagonal half. Rotate it four more 45° steps around the canvas to reach the southeast side; this is step 2 of 5 counterclockwise rotations from the top.

ACTION3

The second left command was blocked, confirming the applicator has a left-tilt limit rather than a full orbit. Reverse toward the right-hand orientation.

ACTION4

The applicator is back at horizontal. Tilt it one step to the right; this should expose the southeast-facing diagonal needed for the yellow target region.

ACTION4

The yellow applicator is now tilted clockwise, aligning its leading edge with the target’s top-right-to-bottom-left diagonal. Stamp the yellow layer.

ACTION5

The clockwise stamp painted the wrong diagonal (`c ≥ r`). Reset the current puzzle, then use the counterclockwise tilt to create the required lower-right anti-diagonal yellow region.

RESET

Reset restored the blank black canvas with red selected and the applicator horizontal. First stamp the red upper half, recreating the correct base layer.

ACTION5

The red upper half is now correctly painted. I’ll test the right/clockwise control to rotate the applicator toward the diagonal needed for the pink lower-right region.

ACTION4

The applicator is now at the required descending diagonal. Select the pink swatch before stamping.

ACTION6 46 4

Pink is selected and the applicator has the correct descending diagonal orientation. Stamp it to overlay the lower-right half and match the target.

ACTION5

The gray stamp produced the wrong diagonal (`\` instead of `/`). Reset the current puzzle so we can change the applicator orientation before repainting.

RESET

First create the target’s horizontal base: the default pink applicator should paint the upper five rows while leaving the black lower half intact.

ACTION5

The pink top half is now correct. Select the blue palette swatch for the diagonal overlay.

ACTION6 46 4

Pink base is preserved and blue is selected. Probe the first directional control to orient the workpiece for the diagonal coat.

ACTION1

ACTION1 was a no-op (likely Up). Test the left/rotation control; the move bar shows ample remaining attempts.

ACTION3

The blue applicator is now aligned with the target’s rising diagonal. Apply it to overlay the lower-right triangle.

ACTION5

The last roll painted the top-left triangle, the mirror image of the target. Reset this level, then we’ll use the opposite tilt before rolling.

RESET

First recreate the required horizontal pink base on the black target; the applicator is in its default orientation.

ACTION5

The pink upper half is now correct. Move the palette selection right from pink to orange.

ACTION4

The applicator is now angled toward the canvas. Select the orange swatch before dispensing.

Orange is loaded in the diagonal applicator; apply it to create the required orange triangular half.

ACTION5

The orange stamp currently faces the upper-right triangular half; test the first orientation control before repainting.

ACTION1

The current stamp produced the wrong `\` diagonal. Test the opposite vertical control; we can reset afterward.

ACTION2

The test confirms directional controls reposition the stamp; clear the experimental paint before applying the mirrored orientation.

RESET

Start from the clean layout by applying the horizontal red stamp; this should create the target’s red upper half.

ACTION5

The red base is correctly applied. Select the gray paint, which will be used for the diagonal overlay.
